finding: Capital One's own Zelle product page, help article and Zelle T&C (dated 4/27/2026) confirm the service; bank-authored evidence outranks the network list.
resolution: zelle: true, evidence CONFIRMED_BANK, sources S001, S049, S076.

claim: Cancel a scheduled one-time (internal) transfer until 11:59 PM ET the day before
finding: The 11:59 PM ET cut-off appears only in the Zelle T&C ('Sending Future Dated Transfers') and the EFT disclosure sentence 'For Zelle Scheduled Payments…'. No Capital One page states a cancel cut-off for internal/external (non-Zelle) scheduled transfers; the gap-fill capture itself notes no help article describes cancelling an Upcoming Transaction.
resolution: Scheduled and recurring transfers appear under 'Upcoming Transactions' and can be cancelled before they run; the UI path and cut-off are not published (the 11:59 PM ET day-before rule is documented only for Zelle Scheduled Payments).

claim: Cancel scheduled one-time external transfer until 11:59 PM ET day before (source S049)
finding: Same misattribution as COF-C002: S049 is the Zelle T&C and its 11:59 PM ET rule governs Zelle future-dated payments only.
resolution: Cancel scheduled one-time/recurring external transfers from Upcoming Transactions; cut-off UNKNOWN (11:59 PM ET rule is Zelle-only).

finding: The current Add-a-payee help article says the account number is required the first time a payee is added; manual payees are paid by paper check, but nothing says the account number may be blank. S019 and S020 are silent on this.
resolution: Payee account number required when first adding a payee; manual (non-directory) payees paid by mailed paper check.

finding: The bank's rule is that the SUBSCRIBER must have a U.S. physical address to set up Bill Pay. The only 'military' language in the 360 Checking disclosure concerns mailing cashier's checks ('except military addresses or P.O. boxes'), not bill-pay payees.

claim: ACH payments free on Basic/Enhanced/Premier Checking and Business Savings
finding: The SMB online-banking page footnote lists only Basic Checking, Enhanced Checking and Business Savings.
resolution: Keep original wording (Basic/Enhanced/Premier Checking and Business Savings).

claim: Name: "Small Business bill pay — 'Accounts Payable with Capital One' / 'Pay Vendors' (Capital One Business)"; note says the $50 late-fee reimbursement and <=$10M sales limit are 'earlier marketing'
finding: The live page is titled 'Accounts Payable with Capital One Business Cards' and pitched to people who already have a Capital One card. Eligibility is 'dynamic'. Separately, the live SMB online-banking page still describes business bill pay (ACH/debit/credit, QuickBooks Online, up to $50 late-fee reimbursement, not for clients with sales above $10M), so those terms are current, not 'earlier'.
resolution: Name: "Accounts Payable with Capital One Business Cards (SMB bill pay / 'Pay Vendors')". Note: marketed as a Business Card benefit and reached inside the Capital One Business account; eligibility 'dynamic'. The SMB online-banking page [S033] currently offers business bill pay (ACH/debit/credit funding, QuickBooks Online, up to $50 late-fee reimbursement, not for clients with annual sales above $10M).

target: COF-J01/EXCEPTION/'Wrong recipient / authorized push payment scam'
finding: Capital One publishes no scam-reimbursement policy and states there is no purchase protection. That part holds. But since 30 June 2023 a Zelle network rule, which applies to every participating bank including owner-bank Capital One, reverses funds for imposter scams (impersonating a government agency, bank or existing provider). 'Likely no reimbursement' leaves out a documented network-level path.
resolution: No Capital One-published scam reimbursement commitment and no purchase protection; victims phone 800-655-2265. Zelle network rules (since 30 June 2023) provide recovery/refund for qualifying imposter scams (government, bank or provider impersonation), assessed case by case; other authorized-payment scams generally not reimbursed.

claim: Overdraft-covering automatic transfer is not modeled
finding: The 360 Checking overdraft options include 'Free transfer', a standing automatic transfer into checking to cover overdrafts, set under More Services > Overdraft Settings. This is a rule-based internal money movement, and the chapter does not mention it.
resolution: Add COF-P02-S06 'Free transfer (automatic overdraft-covering transfer)': set via checking account > More Services > Overdraft Settings; one of three overdraft options (No-fee overdraft, Auto-decline, Free transfer); source account not stated on page.

claim: MONEY Teen parent-to-teen allowance and one-time transfers are not modeled (S911 captured but unused)
finding: The MONEY help article documents a recurring allowance (amount, frequency, day; slide to confirm) and a one-time parent 'send' or teen 'pay you back' transfer, both from the MONEY home screen.
resolution: Add COF-P02-S07 'MONEY teen allowance and parent/teen transfers' [S911].

claim: Chapter does not note that Capital One co-owns Early Warning Services (Zelle and Paze operator)
finding: Capital One is one of the seven owner banks of EWS. the participation baseline participation notes also say 'Zelle/EWS owner'. This is material context for Zelle/Paze positioning and network-rule influence.
resolution: Differentiator: 'Capital One is one of the seven bank owners of Early Warning Services (operator of Zelle and Paze).'

claim: No mention of the June 2026 Zelle cross-border / ZelleUSD announcement
finding: On 2026-06-11 EWS announced Zelle cross-border P2P (India first, before end-2026) and a ZelleUSD (ZLUSD) stablecoin. This bears directly on the chapter's weakness 'no digital international wire or remittance for consumers'. Nothing says whether or when Capital One will offer it.
resolution: Recent change: '2026-06-11: EWS announced Zelle cross-border P2P (India first, planned before end-2026) and a ZelleUSD (ZLUSD) stablecoin; Capital One (an EWS owner) has not announced customer availability.' Plus an open question.

finding: No bank page offers a send-to-card product, so 'no originating product' is a fair inference. But the consolidated the participation baseline participation matrix records push_to_card = 'unknown' for capital-one. A false value from absence of evidence also says nothing about receiving Visa Direct/Mastercard Send credits on Capital One debit cards.
resolution: Both positions stand. Settled by a Capital One disclosure or app screen showing (or ruling out) a debit-card push send, or a Visa Direct/Mastercard Send participant list. Until then, the research dataset and the participation baseline should agree. Recommend the research dataset keep false with scope 'no bank-originated send product' and the participation baseline footnote the scope.

claim: Mobile deposit: checking next-business-day availability; most savings products 4-business-day hold
finding: The live Mobile deposits help article says funds are generally available by the next business day for eligible checking, savings and money market accounts, with no savings carve-out. The Deposit support article still states a 4-business-day hold for most savings deposits. The bank's own pages conflict.
resolution: Record both statements as conflicting bank guidance. Settled by the current Funds Availability Policy for savings products or an authenticated deposit confirmation.

finding: Steps inserted by the gap-fill patch carry step_no 1 or 2 in the middle of journeys (J08: 6 -> 1 -> 2 -> 8; J16: 3 -> 1 -> 4; J21: 3 -> 1 -> 4), so step_no no longer gives order. This is a data-integrity defect from patch application (the patch specified step_no 5 for J16).

claim: No instant outbound option for consumers (no push-to-card, no RTP/FedNow send product marketed)
finding: Zelle is an instant outbound consumer rail at Capital One ('money should typically arrive in minutes'), so 'no instant outbound option' is literally untrue. The real gap is instant transfers to the customer's OWN external accounts and to non-Zelle recipients.
resolution: Beyond Zelle P2P, consumers have no instant outbound option: no push-to-card, no marketed RTP/FedNow send, and transfers to their own external accounts take 1–3 business days by ACH [S008][S007][S001].

claim: Instant payments participation product evidence = CONFIRMED_BANK
finding: Participation rests on operator lists (TCH, FedNow). Capital One's own Jan 2026 'What are instant payments?' explainer does not say Capital One offers them. Product-level CONFIRMED_BANK may overstate.
resolution: Keep COF-P09 evidence CONFIRMED_BANK (receive only); send stays unknown.
